question: ________ refers to sale and purchase of government securities by RBI in the open market with the aim of influencing liquidity in the economy in the medium term.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Open Market Operations.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)** is a **monetary policy tool** used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to manage **liquidity **in the economy.
 
• Through OMO, the RBI **buys or sells government securities** in the open market, which influences the** money supply** in the economy.
 
• OMO can be used to inject liquidity into the system by** purchasing securities**, or to** absorb excess liquidity **by selling securities.
 
• OMO is considered a **medium-term tool** as its impact on liquidity takes a few weeks to materialize.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** is a short-term **borrowing** facility for banks.
 
• **Credit Ceiling** refers to a limit on the amount of credit that can be** extended** by banks.
 
• **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** is a mechanism used by the RBI to manage **short-term liquidity** in the economy by adjusting the** repo rate and reverse repo rate.**
